issues.description: Template Stock.java declares findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) but other methods in the same class (add, take) call findStockIngredient with a single String parameter. This internal mismatch will cause compilation errors and prevents students from using the Stock API as intended.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the findStockIngredient signature consistent with its usages. Either provide an overload findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the two-parameter method, or change the existing definition to findStockIngredient(String name) so add() and take() can call it as-is.

issues.description: The problem specification (UML and textual description) defines Stock.findStockIngredient as taking a single String parameter, but the template Stock.java uses a two-parameter signature. This discrepancy between the specification and template will confuse students about the required API and how to implement or use findStockIngredient.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the specification: change the template's method to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (single parameter) as shown in the UML, or update the problem statement/UML to document the two-parameter variant and provide consistent usage examples. Prefer changing the template to the single-parameter signature to match the UML and solution.

issues.description: The problem text is inconsistent about the stock attribute modifiers: one part instructs a 'final Stock stock' (read-only after construction), while a later note explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). This contradiction could confuse students about whether stock should be an instance final field or a static (class-level) field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: explicitly state that the stock field should be declared static final (class-level, read-only reference) if that is the intended design. Update the earlier sentence to mention static final Stock stock, so both places convey the same requirement.

issues.description: Method signature mismatch for Stock.findStockIngredient: the problem statement (and the solution) describe a single-parameter method findStockIngredient(String), but the template implementation provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with an extra caseSensitive parameter. This creates a mapping confusion: students reading the problem will look for a single-argument method as specified, while the starter code exposes a different signature, increasing extraneous cognitive load and risking incorrect usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Stock API match the problem statement and solution by providing a single-parameter method: add or rename to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (optionally implement it to delegate to the existing two-parameter version). This ensures students can directly map the problem description to the starter code.
